items.t: Harbour Chines is the "Chines" slope of central Coquitlam served by Como Lake Avenue, adjoining the Chineside sub-area. Nearby areas: Chineside to the west/south-west, Central Coquitlam to the east, Ranch Park to the south, and the City Centre / Pinetree Way edge to the north-east.

Current listing evidence for the sub-area is detached houses only — a current listing page for the area describes tree-lined streets of detached homes, with most homes on lots of 10,000 square feet or more.

Main roads: Como Lake Avenue serves the Chines area. Como Lake Park is a City park name in City records for central Coquitlam. The nearest hospital is Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, on the Port Moody / Coquitlam border. The nearest library branch is the Coquitlam Public Library City Centre branch, 1169 Pinetree Way.

items.t: Harbour Chines is a central Coquitlam pocket on the slope above Como Lake Avenue — "chines" being the ravine/valley terrain, and there is no harbour or waterfront in the sub-area despite the name.

Do not merge Chineside: Harbour Chines and Chineside are two separate Coquitlam sub-areas with separate rows in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report. Stats, stock and catchments from one never carry to the other.

Medians are community-level only: Coquitlam "Condos & Townhomes" combined median was $625,000 in September 2026 ($687/sqft, 96% sale-to-list, 23 days on market), and the Coquitlam detached median was $1,455,000.
Transit: no station is inside Harbour Chines; the nearest SkyTrain stations are Coquitlam Central and Burquitlam on the Evergreen Extension (Millennium Line).

School names that appear on listing pages for Harbour Chines houses (including Harbour View Elementary and Dr. Charles Best Secondary) are listing copy, not district-verified catchments — run the exact address in the SD43 School Locator.
Parks: Como Lake Park is a City of Coquitlam park name for the central-Coquitlam Como Lake area.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Harbour Chines

items.t: City zoning and plan (Coquitlam): Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996 — small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3, subdivision minimums 650 m² / 18.5 m width (R-1, R-3) and 465 m² / 12.5 m (R-2). The Interim Official Community Plan — Bylaws 5511/5512, 2026 — was adopted April 27, 2026 and supersedes OCP No. 3479; the interim OCP is the current plan.

Presales (REDMA), if any are ever marketed here: a presale buyer must receive the developer's disclosure statement (REDMA s. 18) and has a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing or acknowledging it (REDMA s. 21), with deposits in trust.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Harbour Chines

items.t: Established house lots: detached houses on the Como Lake slope under the small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3 in Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996. Subdivision minimums are 650 m² with 18.5 m width in R-1 and R-3, and 465 m² with 12.5 m width in R-2. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot. A fee-simple lot carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees.
Serviced position, as the City states it: Coquitlam utility charges cover water, sewer and drainage and solid waste; lots not connected to municipal water or sewer are outside the SSMUH rules.
Check any parcel in the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder.

Watercourse position: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam; Zoning Bylaw s.519 sets flood protection setbacks and s.523 covers riparian areas.
No named bare-land development, assembly, development site or rezoning proposal inside Harbour Chines is confirmed.

Historic subdivision fabric = built lot fabric, not offerings: the Como Lake slope streets are established fee-simple lot fabric documented above; no historic subdivision is presented as a lot offering.
No named presale project of any form in Harbour Chines was confirmed on an official or developer source.

Roads and transit: Como Lake Avenue serves the Chines area. The nearest Evergreen Extension (Millennium Line) stations are Coquitlam Central and Burquitlam.

Schools: SD43 catchments are address-based. Programs of Choice (French Immersion, Mandarin Bilingual, Montessori) and cross-catchment moves are application / lottery processes, never catchment rights.

items.t: If a parcel is in the ALR: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an extra residence can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). For farm class, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.

items.t: The name is the trap: there is no harbour or waterfront in Harbour Chines.
School District 43 Programs of Choice — French Immersion, Mandarin Bilingual and Montessori — are entered by application, not by catchment.
Cross-catchment applications in SD43 are decided by a lottery / random draw with in-district priority.
The nearest library branch is Coquitlam Public Library City Centre at 1169 Pinetree Way, with the Poirier branch at 575 Poirier Street.
The nearest Evergreen Extension (Millennium Line) stations are Coquitlam Central and Burquitlam; no station is inside Harbour Chines.
The Harbour Chines-specific point is the municipality itself: taxes are Coquitlam taxes, due July 2, 2026, not Port Coquitlam taxes.
Coquitlam is listed as a taxable area for the provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax, so every residential owner must complete the annual declaration.
Como Lake Avenue is the street that serves the Chines area of central Coquitlam.
Rapid transit is reached at Coquitlam Central or Burquitlam station on the Evergreen Extension of the Millennium Line, both outside the sub-area.
